content.title: Executive Summary
content.body: Linear is an issue-tracking and product-planning workspace built around teams, projects, cycles, and issues. It is most relevant to software teams considering a focused way to plan and track delivery. Fit depends on whether its workflow model supports the team’s existing process. Ratings, review counts, prices, and plan entitlements are not independently verified here.

content.title: TL;DR
content.body: Evaluate Linear if your software team wants issue tracking connected to planning and delivery. Test custom workflow needs, permission requirements, reporting, and integration coverage early. Teams that rely on highly customized processes should compare alternatives before migrating.

content.title: Feature Evaluation
content.body: Use a representative backlog to test triage, issue ownership, cycle planning, project status, search, notifications, and connections to source control and chat. Verify that the fields and reports your team depends on can be represented without workarounds. Check how changes to workflow conventions affect day-to-day use.

content.title: Who Should Consider It
content.body: Software teams that want issue tracking and product planning in a shared workspace should assess Linear against their delivery process. Teams outside engineering should verify that the model fits their work, and organizations with complex approval or permission needs should test those cases before adoption.

content.title: Limitations to Test
content.body: Test workflow flexibility, custom fields, role permissions, audit needs, reporting, and data export. Migration planning should account for comments, attachments, labels, issue relationships, and history. Confirm which administrative and security controls require a particular plan.

content.title: Pricing Explained
content.body: Current prices, plan limits, and billing terms are not independently verified. Check Linear’s official pricing page and contract for seat rules, guest access, issue or project limits, AI features, integrations, SSO, audit logs, and support entitlements. Compare the full cost for the intended team.

content.title: Security & Privacy Checks
content.body: Request current security and privacy documentation, data-processing terms, retention and export details, identity controls, audit events, and incident-response commitments. Verify plan availability and contractual coverage before importing sensitive issue or customer data.

content.title: Implementation Checklist
content.body: Trial Linear with a small team and a realistic backlog. Import a sample, connect the code-hosting integration, recreate one cycle, test reports and permissions, and document data that does not migrate cleanly. Expand only after the team confirms that the workflow fits.

content.title: Alternatives
content.body: Compare Linear with a more customizable engineering tracker and a broader work-management platform. Run the same backlog and cycle-planning tasks in each, then compare configuration effort, reporting, permissions, integration fit, and migration risk.

content.title: Final Verdict
content.body: Linear is worth evaluating for software teams that prefer a focused issue and product-planning workflow. It may be less suitable where deep workflow customization or complex administrative controls are mandatory. Confirm current plan details and test a realistic migration before deciding.
